in_sanskrit.name: दक्ष
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The word 'Daksh' comes from the Sanskrit root 'daks' which means 'to reach' or 'to touch'. The prefix 'da' in 'Daksh' denotes 'great' or 'excellent'. Hence, the name Daksh means 'the one who is dexterous, skilled or able'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of Rain, is also known as Daksh. He is often depicted as the God of sacrifice and is also considered as the God of wealth.

in_hindi.name: दक्ष
in_hindi.long_meaning: The name 'Daksh' in Hindi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'daksh' which means 'dexterous' or 'skilled'. It is also used as a synonym for the word 'dakshin' which means 'southern' or 'right'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of Rain, is also known as Daksh.

in_tamil.name: தக்ஷ
in_tamil.long_meaning: The name 'Daksh' in Tamil is derived from the Sanskrit word 'daksh' which means 'dexterous' or 'skilled'. The Tamil word 'செயல்' (ceyal) means 'to do' or 'to make', and the word 'விழுது' (vizhuthu) means 'ability' or 'skill'. Hence, the name Daksh can be translated as 'one who has the ability to do things'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of Rain, is also known as Daksh.

in_telugu.name: దక్ష

In Hindu mythology, Lord Indra, the God of Rain, is also known as Daksh.
